preamble: pitfight (formerly the working name bot-arena; CLI command `pit`): a Core War-style programming game. Players write small bots for a tiny virtual machine; the bots share a circular memory arena and try to make each other crash. v1 is the ISA spec, assembler, deterministic VM and arena, tournament runner, replay format, and terminal and web viewers, in Go (standard library only) with a plain JavaScript + canvas web viewer. Source: PROJECT.md and the owner decisions of 2026-10-15 (C26-C37).

note_records.text: **2026-10-15** — **2026-10-15** — From S03 review: isa.md §8 replicator sketch keeps one process (the original dies at cell 5); the starter replicator should loop back instead of DAT so it multiplies.

**2026-10-18** — S10 closing note. Four original starter bots (bots/imp.s, dwarf.s, replicator.s, scanner.s), tests in internal/arena/bots_test.go and golden_test.go. Decisions C80 (golden table shape), C81 (bot designs and parameters), C82 (bots/ ships in release archives), C90 (scanner lap blind spot). No ISA findings: all four strategies are expressible.

Golden values (default config, seeds 1/2/3, lower id first), how each was reviewed by hand. Cross-check: a separate Python implementation of SplitMix64, placement and the VM, written from isa.md and match.md only, with bot cells hand-transcribed from the sources, reproduced all 18 rows exactly (starts, cycles, winner). Then per row:
- imp vs dwarf (imp moves first). The imp runs the cell it just wrote, so only a bomb landing exactly on that cell kills it. Dwarf bomb k lands in cycle 3k-1 at dwarf_start+3+4k; the imp head is at imp_start+t after cycle t; they meet at k = (imp_start - dwarf_start - 4) mod 8000. Seed 1: 4519-2555-4 = 1960, bomb in cycle 5879, imp dies in cycle 5880 (pinned 5880, winner 2; imp would reach the dwarf only at cycle 6036). Seed 2: 5432-4226-4 = 1202, cycle 3605, death in 3606 (pinned 3606, winner 2). Seed 3: the imp reaches the dwarf code at cycle 3140, before the meeting at k=4856, and overwrites it with imps; no DAT is executed, tie at 80000.
- dwarf vs scanner. Seed 1 (2959, winner 1): dwarf bomb 986 (cycle 2957) hits scanner cell 0 at 466; the scanner runs cell 0 when the cycle is 1 mod 3, so it executes the DAT in cycle 2959. Seed 2 (3990, winner 1): bomb 1001 (cycle 3002) hits scanner cell 2 (the MOV); the scanner finds dwarf cell 2 at pass 1330 (4233+3*1330 = 8223 = 223 mod 8000) and executes the bombed cell in cycle 3990. Seed 3 (2138, winner 2): the scanner finds dwarf cell 1 at pass 712 and bombs it in cycle 2136; the dwarf runs JMP in 2136, ADD in 2137, the DAT in 2138; the dwarf's own first hit on the scanner would be in cycle 4391.
- imp vs scanner and imp vs replicator (all 6 rows, ties at 80000): in the independent simulator the imp never executes a DAT, and the other bot keeps processes (scanner 1; replicator 108, 68, 117 at the end for seeds 1-3). Imp vs scanner executes no DAT at all: the scanner pointer stays a constant distance behind the imp head, or loses ground when it finds trail cells, so it cannot bomb the head. Checked by trace, not by closed form for every lap restart.
- dwarf vs replicator (2334, 2896, 5425; winner 1). Copies sit 100 cells apart, so the dwarf's stride-4 bombs hit the same two cells of every copy: c = (dwarf start + 3 - replicator start) mod 4, and c+4. That is cells 2 and 6 at seeds 1 and 2, cells 3 and 7 at seed 3 (dwarf 7564, replicator 4373). The replicator never writes the dwarf's cells. Last death checked per seed against the bomb formula (bomb k at cycle 3k-1 on ptr+4k): seed 1 k=776, cycle 2327, cell 7626, last replicator death cycle 2334; seed 2 k=965, cell 5872, death 2896; seed 3 k=1806, cell 6788, death 5425.
- replicator vs scanner (12099, 1046, 14208; winner 1): rests on the independent simulation and a trace, not a closed-form derivation. The replicator out-multiplies the scanner's bombs and its copy loops overwrite a scanner cell with an empty cell. Seed 1: bot 1's MOV.I at cycle 12099 copies an empty cell (source 7448) onto 7532, scanner cell 0, which the scanner then runs as DAT. Seed 2: written in cycle 1045 onto 4226, scanner dies in 1046.

Mutation checks (bots/test restored after each): imp target changed (TestImp); dwarf stride 5, bomb DAT.F #1 (after pinning the bomb cell explicitly), bomb NOP, JMP into ptr (TestDwarf); replicator JMP replaced by DAT, source count -7, SPL fixed at +100 (TestReplicator); scanner stride 2, bomb onto ptr, SNE for SEQ (TestScanner); stray bots/extra.s, bad modifier, temporary Disassemble B+1 (TestStarterBotsAssemble); dwarf stride 5, scanner stride 2, imp to JMP, replicator ADD #104 (TestGolden, many rows red). A first replicator hard-coded SPL start+100 and TestReplicator caught it (second spawn at the wrong address).

Known limits: scanner blind spot (C90): a lap examines relative cells 10..7807, so enemy code lying only in cells 7808..7899 (inside placement's guaranteed-empty gap) is never examined. Replicator copies collide on the 100-cell lattice and share one ptr per site, so some processes aim at garbage and die (first such death at cycle 112 in every replicator match); the golden rows are sensitive to this by design.

records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15. No map iteration in the VM or arena core (Go map order is randomized). Randomness comes only from an in-repo seeded PRNG with a fixed, documented algorithm, not math/rand or math/rand/v2, so results and replays survive Go upgrades. Extends C12 and C03.

records.title: pit usage handling: stderr+exit 2 for no args or unknown subcommand, help on stdout
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S02). `pit` with no arguments prints usage to stderr and exits 2; `pit help` prints usage to stdout and exits 0; an unknown subcommand prints `pit: unknown subcommand "X"`, a blank line and the usage to stderr, exit 2. The usage lists asm, run, tourney, view and help as planned, and states exit codes 0 success, 2 usage error (1 is reserved for a failed operation in later slices). Planned subcommands that are not built yet also report unknown. Reason: it matches the slice text and the shell convention that usage errors are 2 and requested help is 0; the planned-not-built case disappears as each subcommand lands.

records.title: scripts/env.sh needs bash or zsh and refuses to run outside a repo root
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S02), accepted by the owner 2026-10-15, overriding the slice's 'POSIX sh, no bashisms' text. A sourced POSIX script cannot learn its own path, so env.sh reads BASH_SOURCE or zsh's %x, derives the repo root from it, clears CDPATH for the cd, and exports nothing and creates nothing unless that root holds go.mod and scripts/env.sh (otherwise it prints an error and returns 1; dash fails the same way). It is sourced by absolute path from anywhere. Reason: the cache directories must follow the checkout (each worktree has its own .cache/) and a wrong or copied env.sh must never write Go caches elsewhere. env.sh does not set GOFLAGS=-modcacherw (the module has no dependencies); a slice that adds an approved dependency should revisit that.

records.title: ISA opcode set: 15 opcodes, codes in table order, no MOD or CMP
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S03). Opcodes in code order: DAT MOV ADD SUB MUL DIV JMP JMZ JMN DJN SPL SEQ SNE SLT NOP (codes 0..14). No MOD, LDP, STP or CMP alias. All 7 modifiers and 8 modes are valid with every opcode. Reason: the smallest Redcode-like set that still expresses imp, bomber, replicator and scanner, which keeps the spec to a few pages (C27, PROJECT.md); the code order is the order of the Go constants in internal/isa. Defined in docs/spec/isa.md section 3.

records.title: ISA modifiers and addressing-mode tokens: A B AB BA F X I; # $ * @ { < } >
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S03). Modifier mnemonics A B AB BA F X I (codes 0..6) and mode tokens # $ * @ { < } > (codes 0..7), with Redcode field pairing and mode meanings; I acts as F except for MOV, SEQ and SNE, where it covers the whole cell. DAT, JMP, SPL and NOP ignore the modifier. Reason: the owner chose an ISA strongly inspired by Redcode semantics (C27); familiar tokens let later Redcode compatibility reuse them and need no new vocabulary. docs/spec/isa.md section 3.

records.title: ISA numbers: CORESIZE 1..2^20, stored values int32 in [0,CORESIZE), arithmetic in int64
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S03). 1 <= CORESIZE <= 1048576; Norm(x) = ((x mod N) + N) mod N in int64; stored operand values are int32 in [0,N); written values are any integer, stored as Norm. Reason: int64 intermediates make ADD, SUB and MUL (up to 2^40) overflow-free for every allowed size, and the range includes the sizes 1, 8 and 8000 that the S05 tests name. docs/spec/isa.md section 1.

records.title: ISA empty cell is DAT.F $0, $0 with writer 0; bot ids start at 1
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S03). A fresh core cell is DAT.F $0, $0, writer 0 (no bot); bot ids are 1 and up; the writer is metadata that no instruction reads and SEQ.I/SNE.I ignore. Every cell write, including pre-decrement, post-increment and DJN decrement writes, sets the writer to the executing bot. Reason: matches the Redcode empty cell and makes unwritten core visible to the visualizer as owner 0 without a special value. docs/spec/isa.md section 2 and 4.

records.title: ISA step semantics: A then B evaluation with snapshots, post-increments after execute
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S03). A step fetches a copy IR, evaluates A (with pre-decrement writes) then B, taking a snapshot of each target at evaluation time; an immediate operand targets the executing cell; both operands are always evaluated; the opcode writes at most one cell; post-increments of A then B apply after execution, even if the process dies; then the process effect is appended. Reason: one fixed order makes events and worked cases unambiguous for the VM, replay and visualizer. Post-increment timing may differ from Redcode and is flagged in the spec. docs/spec/isa.md section 4.

records.title: ISA faults: only DAT and division by zero kill; DIV writes nothing if any divisor is 0
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S03). A process dies only by executing DAT or by DIV with a zero divisor in any of its pairs; in that case DIV writes nothing for any pair. Every cell content is legal, so there is no illegal-instruction fault. Reason: a single all-or-nothing rule is simpler to specify and test than Redcode's per-pair partial write. docs/spec/isa.md section 5.

records.title: ISA SPL at the process limit acts as a continue-only NOP
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S03). SPL appends PC+1 then the A target; if the bot already has MAXPROCESSES live processes (the executing one counts), only PC+1 is appended and nothing is signalled. The value and range of MAXPROCESSES are left to the match spec (S04). Reason: a failed spawn must not kill or error the bot, and the executing process counts so the cap is exact. docs/spec/isa.md section 5.

records.title: ISA spec table format and worked-case format (parsed by S06)
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S03). Three tables, each with header first column Mnemonic, the exact assembler token in backticks, rows in code order from 0 (opcodes, modifiers, addressing modes); no other table starts with Mnemonic. Worked cases are tables headed Case | Setup | Before | After | Queue; the Case id is OPCODE.MODIFIER[/suffix] or a mode mnemonic[/suffix]; Setup is N=<core size>[, MAXPROCESSES=<n>]; Before lists address: cell separated by semicolons with unlisted cells empty; After lists each write in order; Queue lists the addresses appended, [] for a dead bot. Reason: S06 parses these tables, so a fixed machine-readable layout lets it check that every entry has a test. Cases were checked against a scratch reference stepper outside the repo. docs/spec/isa.md sections 3 and 6.

records.title: Match defaults confirmed: core 8000, cycle limit 80000, max processes 8000
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S04). Verifies C30 on 2026-10-15: all three values are stated as defaults in the ICWS'94 draft predefined variables (https://corewar.info/lexicon/94draft.htm: CORESIZE 8000, MAXCYCLES 80000, MAXPROCESSES 8000) and on the 94 Standard Hill page (http://www.corewar.info/hills/94.htm: core size 8000, max cycles 80000, max processes 8000); the pMARS manual (https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/noble/man6/pmars.6.html) confirms 8000 for -s and -p and gives no -c default. Ranges: CORESIZE 1..2^20, CYCLELIMIT 1..2^31-1, MAXPROCESSES 1..2^20, MINSEPARATION 0..2^20, SEED any uint64 (default 0). Reason: two independent public sources agree on each value, so C30 no longer needs its unverified flag. docs/spec/match.md sections 1 and 2.

records.title: Match PRNG: SplitMix64, seed uint64, rejection-sampled Draw(n)
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 and C36 (S04). Generator is fixed-increment SplitMix64 (state += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15; two xor-shift-multiply rounds with 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9 and 0x94D049BB133111EB; final xor-shift 31), seed any uint64 including 0, all arithmetic modulo 2^64. Draw(n) for uint64 n>=1 rejects outputs below (2^64-n) mod n, so there is no modulo bias, and always consumes at least one output. Reason: a few lines of integer-only code with one 64-bit state and a published public-domain reference (https://prng.di.unimi.it/splitmix64.c), and rejection sampling removes modulo bias at the cost of a rule that is still easy to state exactly. Test vectors for seeds 0, 1 and 2^64-1 and rejection cases are in docs/spec/match.md section 4.

records.title: Tie rule: sole survivor wins; otherwise a tie among the last live bots
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 and C38 (S04). After the last cycle, exactly one live bot wins; two or more survivors at the cycle limit tie (tied = survivors); no survivor (all remaining bots died in the last cycle) is a tie among the bots live at the start of that cycle. No tiebreak by process count or owned cells. Reason: it keeps the pMARS manual's 'single warrior remains' win and 'both lasted until time-out' tie, and treats bots that die in the same complete cycle as equal because each took the same number of steps. docs/spec/match.md section 8.

records.title: Default min separation: 100 empty cells between neighbouring bots
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 and C38 (S04). MINSEPARATION is the minimum count of unowned cells between the end of one bot's block and the start of the next, going around the circular core; default 100, range 0..2^20. Placement is possible if and only if total bot length + bots * MINSEPARATION <= CORESIZE, else the error 'placement impossible: ...'. Reason: 100 is the default of the pMARS -d option and ICWS'94 draft MINDISTANCE (https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/noble/man6/pmars.6.html), which pMARS measures between the first instructions of two warriors; pitfight deliberately counts empty cells between blocks instead, which makes impossibility an exact sum test independent of bot length and is stricter than 100 start-to-start. docs/spec/match.md sections 2 and 6.

records.title: Placement algorithm: shuffle, rotation, sequential gap draws; no retries
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S04). With the seeded generator: Fisher-Yates shuffle of bot ids (draws Draw(i+1) for i=K-1..1), rotation Draw(CORESIZE), then gaps g[k]=Draw(R+1) for k=0..K-2 from remaining slack R with the last gap taking the rest, start of each bot = previous start + length + MINSEPARATION + gap; 2K-1 draws, always made. Reason: it is deterministic and bounded, never needs a retry loop, and is exact for any input that passes the feasibility sum, so two implementations agree; the gap distribution is documented as non-uniform. Worked placements and impossible cases in docs/spec/match.md section 6.

records.title: Turn order: all live bots step once per cycle in ascending id; match ends at end of cycle
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 and C38 (S04). A cycle is one step for each bot live at its start, in ascending bot id (ids = input order, not rotated); the match ends after the first cycle that leaves at most one live bot or that is cycle CYCLELIMIT; at least 2 and at most 2^20 bots; loaded cells carry the owner's bot id as writer; each bot starts with one process at its entry offset. Result fields: cycles, survivors, outcome (win or tie), winner, tied. Reason: it follows the pMARS definition of a cycle as one execution of each warrior and checking at the cycle end gives every bot the same number of steps; fixed id order is the simplest rule and fairness across orders is left to the tournament runner. docs/spec/match.md sections 5, 7 and 8.

records.title: isa package API: Opcode/Modifier/Mode uint8 types with Op*/Mod*/Mode* constants in spec order, Opcodes/Modifiers/Modes lists, String() mnemonics, Cell{Opcode,Modifier,AMode,AValue int32,BMode,BValue int32,Writer uint32}, EmptyCell
records.body: Plain typed constants and exported slices give later enumeration tests and the assembler one source for codes and mnemonics; int32 values and uint32 writer match isa.md section 1-2; no maps (C36).

records.title: vm core API: NewCore(size) (*Core, error) with ErrCoreSize, Size, Norm(int64) int32, Read(int64) Cell, Write(int64, Cell, bot uint32)
records.body: Addresses are int64 and Core.Norm is the single normalization (spec section 1), so sums cannot overflow and callers need no pre-reduction; Write sets the writer from the bot argument, Read never changes it; out-of-range size is an error rather than a panic.

records.title: vm operand API: Core.Resolve(pc, mode, value, bot) (Operand{Target, Snapshot, Post}, error) and Core.ApplyPostInc(PostInc, bot)
records.body: Splitting evaluation from post-increment lets S06 follow isa.md section 4 (evaluate A, evaluate B, execute, then post-increments on the field as it is in the core then); Resolve applies pre-decrements immediately as bot and returns ErrBadMode for a mode code above 7 instead of panicking.

records.title: VM execution and process queue API
records.body: S06 implementer decision under C35: Core.NewQueue(max, pcs...) returns (*Queue,error), normalizes initial addresses, validates MAXPROCESSES 1..2^20 and initial count, and copies input; Queue exposes Len, Dead and caller-owned Addresses. Core.Step(queue, bot, events) appends value events and executes one FIFO process, with dead queues a no-op. Queue uses a circular slice bounded by max for O(1) removal/requeue. Queues belong to their creating core and must not be copied; Step requires valid ISA codes and normalized cell fields and a nonzero bot id, matching the spec domain. Reason: arena can own one queue per bot, preserve deterministic FIFO order, and reuse its event buffer without shifting up to a million processes each turn.

records.title: VM integer event records and ordering
records.body: S06 implementer decision under C35: Event contains Kind (uint8 EventKind: CellWrite=0, ProcessSpawn=1, ProcessDeath=2), Bot uint32, PC int32, Address int32 and Cell isa.Cell. CellWrite holds the complete post-write cell including writer; process events have zero Cell. PC identifies the executed instruction, Address the written cell, child PC or dead PC. Only actual SPL child creation emits spawn; continuations and denied spawns emit nothing. All cell writes, including equal-value writes, appear in spec phase order; process events follow A/B post-increments. Reason: plain integer values retain intermediate writes for replay without I/O or clocks; caller-owned buffers avoid imposing event storage on the VM.

records.title: LICENSE present; README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md added; SPDX header on Go and shell files
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 and C32 (2026-10-17, owner-requested docs setup). LICENSE holds the AGPL-3.0 text per C32; NOTICE's last line points to it and AGENTS.md records its source and that it is never edited. README.md gives the overview, status, checks and license; CONTRIBUTING.md summarizes AGENTS.md rules and slicer use; PROJECT.md gets a background-only note at the top, body unchanged. Every Go file and scripts/env.sh start with SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later. Reason: the owner asked for the license and contributor docs; AGENTS.md stays the source of truth for agents.

records.title: asm API: Assemble(name, src) (Program{Cells, Entry}, error) with *asm.Error{File,Line,Col,Msg}
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S07). Assemble returns a Program holding the isa.Cell slice and the entry offset, and the first error as *asm.Error whose text is file:line:col: message (line and col start at 1, col counts bytes); on error the Program is the zero value. Reason: match.md section 5 needs an entry offset next to the cells, so a bare []isa.Cell would lose it; one error is enough for a bot file and keeps the first-error order well defined.

records.title: asm syntax: ';' comments, 'label:' definitions, case-insensitive opcodes/modifiers/ORG, case-sensitive labels, opcode[.mod] [A[, B]]
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S07, docs/spec/asm.md sections 1-4). One statement per line; any number of 'name:' labels before it; a label names the next instruction (or the program length if none follows); label names may not be an opcode or ORG; modes # $ * @ { < } > precede the operand expression, default $; an omitted operand is $0. Reason: the colon removes the Redcode ambiguity between a label and an opcode and is easy to lex by hand; the rest follows common Redcode practice.

records.title: asm default modifier: Redcode '94 table without MOD
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 4). DAT and NOP: F; MOV, SEQ, SNE: AB if A is #, else B if B is #, else I; ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV: AB, B, else F; SLT: AB if A is #, else B; JMP, JMZ, JMN, DJN, SPL: B. Reason: isa.md leaves the default to the assembler (section 2) and the Redcode '94 table lets the starter bots be written without explicit modifiers.

records.title: asm expressions: + - * / % and unary +/-, parentheses, labels relative to the instruction, int32 range
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 6). Precedence: unary, then * / %, then binary + -, left-associative; decimal literals only; / and % truncate toward zero like Go; division by zero and any result outside int32 (a literal may be 2147483648 so the minimum can be written) is an error; a label's value is index(label) - index(instruction holding the operand), and in ORG it is the absolute index; expression height is limited to 256. Reason: the smallest set that writes offsets and label differences, with one documented range that makes int64 arithmetic overflow-free.

records.title: asm output cells keep operand values as written (signed int32), not normalized to CORESIZE
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 6). The assembler does not know CORESIZE, and match.md section 5 stores Norm(v) when the bot is loaded, so Cell.AValue and BValue from Assemble may be negative. Reason: keeps a program independent of the core size and keeps listings and the round trip exact.

records.title: asm entry offset: the ORG expression directive, default 0, must lie in 0..L-1
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 5), answering the S04 note. 'ORG expression' on any line, at most once, with labels as absolute indexes; Program.Entry carries the value; without ORG it is 0. Reason: match.md section 5 needs an entry offset e in [0, L) and isa.md has none; ORG is the Redcode name for it.

records.title: asm errors: first error only, syntax errors before evaluation errors, fixed message texts and positions
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 7). Assembly stops at the first error; syntax errors are found in source order while reading, then undefined labels, evaluation errors, the empty program and the ORG range in the order asm.md lists; each message text and its position is a documented table that TestErrors checks. Reason: C17 asks for line and column errors, and fixed texts make them testable; one error per run avoids cascades.

records.title: pit asm <file>: prints a re-assemblable listing (ORG line, one canonical instruction per line); exit 1 on error, 2 on usage
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 9). On success stdout gets 'ORG e' then 'OPCODE.MODIFIER <mode><value>, <mode><value>' per cell with signed decimal values and explicit modifiers, nothing else; an assembly error or unreadable file prints file:line:col: message (or 'pit asm: <os error>') on stderr and exits 1 with empty stdout; a wrong argument count or an argument starting with '-' prints 'usage: pit asm <file>' and exits 2. The file name is printed exactly as given. The usage text now lists asm as implemented, marks the other commands 'not implemented yet' and adds exit code 1. Reason: a listing is both human-readable and valid source, which the S08 round trip needs; the exit codes extend C40.

records.title: pit run flags: --seed, --core-size, --cycle-limit, --max-processes, --min-separation, --json (S09)
records.body: Kebab-case flag per match.md config field, defaults from the spec; flags and bot files may be interleaved (pit run a.s b.s --seed 1) because that is the form the slice and the harness use.

records.title: pit run text output: config line, one line per bot, cycles, survivors, result (S09)
records.body: Plain line-oriented text with the fields of match.md section 8 plus each bot's file, length, start and entry_address (the absolute address Norm(start + entry offset) of its first process, not the offset e of match.md section 5), so a human and grep can read it; byte-identical for the same input (C16). Owner amendment 2026-10-18: the field was called 'entry'; it is entry_address (done in S11). With --replay S11 adds a last line 'replay: <hash>' (see the S11 record).

records.title: pit run --json: one JSON line with config, bots, cycles, survivors, outcome, winner, tied (S09)
records.body: A single line of fixed-order snake_case JSON with lists never null is the simplest machine-readable form for the later agent harness (C09). Owner amendment 2026-10-18 (done in S11): seed is a decimal string, not a JSON number, because JavaScript loses precision above 2^53; the bot field 'entry' is renamed entry_address (the absolute address, not the offset). With --replay a last field replay_hash is added.

records.title: pit run exit codes and error output (S09)
records.body: 0 the match ran (win or tie); 1 a bot file, assembler, config or placement error, printed as 'pit run: <spec message>' on stderr with assembler errors bare as file:line:col like pit asm; 2 a usage error, so scripts can tell a bad invocation from a bad bot.

records.title: arena API: arena.Run(cfg, bots) returns Result, []vm.Event, error (S09)
records.body: Bot is cells plus entry offset so arena does not import the assembler; Result adds the Placement used; events cover steps only, not loading, leaving the replay slice free to choose its initial-state record; errors are *arena.Error with the three kinds of match.md section 1.

records.title: Disassembly is asm.Disassemble(Program) []byte; pit asm is its CLI entry point
records.body: Disassemble takes the Program (cells and entry) so the ORG line survives the round trip, and is the only listing formatter (moved from cmd/pit per C72); Writer is ignored. Reason: no binary cell format or cell source other than assembled source exists, so a separate pit disasm subcommand would print the same bytes as pit asm; documented in docs/spec/asm.md sections 8 and 9.

records.title: isa.md section 8 listings are asm blocks without the N: prefix
records.body: The three starter-bot listings in docs/spec/isa.md are tagged asm and the N: prefix moved into the trailing comment (; N: text), so TestRoundTripSpecExamples can extract and assemble them; the cells are unchanged.

records.title: Replay file: hand-written canonical JSON lines; the reader accepts only the writer's bytes (S11)
records.body: S11 implementer decision under C35 (docs/spec/replay.md sections 1, 4, 8). The writer appends integers with strconv and fixed words by hand, so no map, no encoding/json and no string escaping touch the bytes (C36); the only strings are fixed words, the decimal seed and lowercase-hex hashes. The reader decodes each line with encoding/json for validation, then requires the line to equal what the writer would write for the parsed values, so Read then Write returns the same bytes and the file hash identifies the match. Line order: header, one load line per bot, cycle groups, end. Reason: byte stability across Go versions and one accepted spelling per replay; the cost is that hand-edited replays with other spacing are refused.

records.title: Replay v1 vocabulary: header, load, c/x/w/s/d body lines, end; a c line for every cycle and an x line for every step (S11)
records.body: S11 implementer decision under C35 (replay.md section 4), amended by the owner's 2026-10-18 per-step execute record. Header: version, config (snake_case, seed a decimal string per the owner's C77 amendment), bots with id, hash, length, start, entry_address. load: the bot's Norm'd cells, so the file holds the initial core (C79 left the initial state to the replay). Body: c {n} for EVERY cycle 1..cycles (a cycle always has a step, since the match runs only while two bots are live); inside it one x {b,pc} line for EVERY step, silent ones (JMP, NOP, skipping tests) included, in ascending bot id; the step's events follow its x line and carry no bot or pc: w {a,c:[six ints]}, s {a}, d (no fields; its address is the step's pc), with at most one s or d and it last. A cell is [opcode,modifier,a_mode,a_value,b_mode,b_value] as isa codes, the writer being the step's bot. end: cycles (equal to the last c), survivors, outcome, winner, tied. All numbers stay below 2^31. The reader also checks that a bot steps only while its process count (1 + s - d) is above 0 and that survivors are the bots with a count above 0. Reason: compact (C07) and JS-safe (C19); a viewer rebuilds the core and shows the execution pointers of every cycle (S12, S15) without re-simulating; dropping b and pc from events removes redundancy. Size: the default-limit imp-vs-dwarf replay (5880 cycles) is 782675 bytes, about 133 bytes per cycle for two bots.

records.title: Replay v1 has no snapshot lines; seeking is the viewer's job (S11)
records.body: S11 implementer decision under C35 (replay.md section 5). A viewer that wants to jump to a cycle keeps its own checkpoints while reading the file; a snapshot every K cycles would add up to CORESIZE cells per snapshot and would be a format change. Adding snapshot lines later is a new version number (replay.md section 7), with no optional fields in v1. Reason: smallest format that satisfies the slice; a later version can add them if a viewer needs it.

records.title: Replay hashes: SHA-256 hex of the file bytes; bot hash over entry offset plus raw assembled cells (S11)
records.body: S11 implementer decision under C35 (replay.md section 6). Replay hash: SHA-256 of the whole file including the final line feed, lowercase hex. Bot hash: SHA-256 of the entry offset (4 bytes big endian) then 12 bytes per assembled cell (opcode, modifier, a_mode, a_value int32, b_mode, b_value int32, big endian; writer excluded), using the raw signed values of C69 so the hash does not depend on CORESIZE or placement. Readers treat the bot hash as opaque because the load lines are normalized. Reason: the slice asked for a stated encoding over the assembled cells; raw values keep a bot's identity independent of the match configuration.

records.title: Replay API: replay.Record, Read, Bytes, Hash, BotHash and Player (S11)
records.body: S11 implementer decision under C35. Record(cfg, bots) runs the match and returns a Replay holding the config, bots as loaded, cycles (each with its []arena.Step) and the result; Bytes/Write give the file, Hash(data) and BotHash the hashes; Read(r) validates the whole file and returns a nil replay on any error, with *VersionError for an unknown version (message names the version); Player (NewPlayer, AdvanceTo, Core, Cycle, Steps, Live) rebuilds the core, the live process counts and the executed addresses of the current cycle by applying the file forward, which is what TestReplayEquivalence checks against the live core and live steps. Reason: one in-memory form shared by the pit run writer and later viewers, with no re-simulation.

records.title: arena.RunObserved: per-cycle hook with the live core; Run is built on it (S11)
records.body: S11 implementer decision under C35, following the S09 note on C79 and amended for the per-step execute record. RunObserved(cfg, bots, observe) calls observe(0, core, nil) after loading and observe(c, core, steps) after each cycle with that cycle's []arena.Step in ascending bot id: Step{Bot, PC, Events}, PC being the address the step executed (the front of the bot's queue before it) and Events the step's VM events, empty for a silent step. The buffers are reused; observe must not modify the core or keep anything past the call. Run is RunObserved collecting the events, so its results and events are unchanged. To read the pc of a step the VM gets Queue.Front() (non-test vm source, one line). Reason: a flat event list cannot give cycle boundaries or the pc of steps that emit no event, and the equivalence test needs the live core and live steps at every cycle.

records.title: pit run --replay FILE writes the replay and prints its hash: 'replay: <hash>' or JSON replay_hash (S11)
records.body: S11 implementer decision under C35. The flag name --replay FILE follows the kebab-case flags of C75. With it, pit run records the match, writes FILE (a refused match writes nothing; a write error exits 1 with empty stdout) and adds the replay hash: a last text line 'replay: <64 hex>' and, with --json, a last field replay_hash; without the flag both are absent. Reason: C16 asks for the same result and replay hash on every run; printing the hash lets a script compare runs without shasum.

records.title: Starter golden table shape (S10)
records.body: Golden table pins the 6 unordered pairs of the four starter bots (lower id first, in the order imp, dwarf, replicator, scanner) at seeds 1, 2, 3 under the default config, 18 rows; the reverse order is the tournament's job (match.md section 7), and the table is small enough to review by hand.

records.title: Starter bot designs and parameters (S10)
records.body: Starter bots: dwarf bombs every 4th cell (3-cycle loop, separate bomb cell); replicator is 8 code cells plus an uncopied ptr cell, copies to +100, SPLs to the copy and loops back to copy 100 cells further; scanner examines every 3rd cell for 2600 passes per lap (7800 of 8000 cells, short of its own cells) and bombs with an empty cell. Parameters assume the default 8000-cell core; each is a plain source constant a later slice may tune.

records.title: Ship bots/ in release archives (S10)
records.body: Release archives include bots/ because README tells users to run pit run bots/imp.s bots/dwarf.s; build-release.sh copies the directory into each archive.

records.title: Starter scanner lap blind spot (S10)
records.body: The scanner's 2600-pass lap examines relative cells 10..7807, leaving 7808..7899 (inside placement's guaranteed-empty gap of 7900..7999) a ~92 cell blind spot for enemy code lying wholly there; accepted for the starter bot to keep it from examining its own cells; refines C81.

records.title: Tournament scoring: win 3, tie 1 each, loss 0; rank by points, wins, name (S13)
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 and C38 (S13). A won match scores 3 points, each bot of a tied match 1, a lost match 0; the scoreboard ranks by more points, then more wins, then the bot name in byte order, so no two bots share a rank. Reason: 3/1/0 is the usual Core War hill convention, keeps a tie worth less than half a win-and-loss pair so decisive bots rank above bots that only draw (the imp ties most matches), and the wins and name tiebreaks make the order total and independent of file order. docs/spec/tourney.md section 3.

records.title: Tournament pairings: every pair in both orders each round, one seed per round (S13)
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S13), answering the S04 note. Pairs are the unordered pairs of the name-sorted bots; each round plays every pair twice, as (a,b) then (b,a), so each bot is id 1 (first mover, match.md section 7) as often as id 2; all matches of a round use that round's seed. Reason: match ids are not rotated, so playing both orders is the simplest neutraliser and needs no change to the arena; a shared round seed keeps the two orders of a pair comparable. Matches are numbered along this fixed list, which is also the order results are scored and printed in (C36). docs/spec/tourney.md section 2.

records.title: Tournament seeds: Seed(round) = first SplitMix64 output seeded with the round number, rounds from 1 (S13)
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 and C36 (S13). Seed(r) is Next() of the match.md section 4 generator seeded with r, for r = 1..R; Seed(1)=10451216379200822465, Seed(2)=10905525725756348110. Reason: a pure function of the round with no clock and no math/rand, reusing the in-repo generator so it survives Go upgrades, and mixing spreads consecutive rounds over the whole 64-bit range instead of handing the placement small adjacent seeds. docs/spec/tourney.md section 2.

records.title: pit tourney flags and exit codes (S13)
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S13). pit tourney [flags] <dir>: --rounds N (default 100, the C18 acceptance count), --jobs N (default runtime.NumCPU; changes speed, never output), the four match config flags of pit run (--core-size, --cycle-limit, --max-processes, --min-separation; no --seed, rounds supply seeds), --json and --matches FILE; flags and the directory in any order. Bots are the *.s files directly in the directory, sorted by name and named without .s. Exit 0 ran, 1 directory, bot, config or file error, 2 usage (including rounds or jobs below 1). Reason: mirrors pit run (C75, C78) so one set of habits works for both, and the default 100 makes the C18 command short. docs/spec/tourney.md sections 1, 5 and 6.

records.title: pit tourney output: text scoreboard; --json scoreboard lines; --matches per-match JSON lines with decimal-string seeds (S13)
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 and C39 (S13). Default output is a config line, a scoring line and a right-aligned table (rank, bot, points, played, wins, ties, losses, mean_cycles); --json prints one object per bot (rank, bot, points, played, wins, ties, losses, cycles, mean_cycles); --matches FILE writes one object per match (index, round, seed, first, second, outcome, winner or null, cycles). Seeds are decimal strings (owner decision on C77). Both JSON forms are JSON lines with the same keys on every line. Reason: results stay as files with no database (C39) and uniform lines load straight into DuckDB read_json; the worker count is not printed so the bytes are the same for any --jobs. docs/spec/tourney.md section 5.

records.title: tourney package API: Pairings, Matches, Seed, Run(cfg, bots, rounds, jobs), Score, Format* (S13)
records.body: Implementer decision under C35 (S13). internal/tourney exports Pair/Pairings(n), Match/Matches(n, rounds), Seed(round), Bot{Name, Bot}, MatchResult{Match, Cycles, Winner (bot index, -1 for a tie)}, Run(arena.Config, []Bot, rounds, jobs) ([]MatchResult, error), Standing, Score(bots, results), and FormatText, FormatJSON and FormatMatches. Run uses a fixed-size goroutine pool fed match indexes over a channel; each worker writes only its own result slot, and an error is the one of the lowest failing match index. Reason: results are kept by match index, never by completion order or map iteration (C36), and the formatters live next to Score so a test can compare the exact scoreboard bytes across worker counts without the CLI.

records.title: Viewer frame model: cycle, owners, executed, live
records.body: S12 (C35). internal/tui Frame = {cycle, owners[addr] = last writer id (0 none), executed = [{bot, pc}] of that cycle in ascending bot order, live[bot-1] = process count: 1 at the start plus spawns minus deaths}; only the reported live value is clamped at 0, the running count after each event is not (the player keeps it below 0 when a replay has more deaths than processes). Plain JSON in testdata/viewer/frames.json so the web viewer (S15) can compare. Reason: an x record names only the stepping process, so executed addresses per cycle are all a viewer can know; the model is independent of the renderer (C19).

records.title: Viewer input: line-mode commands s, b, g, p, q
records.body: S12 (C35). pit view reads one command per line from stdin: s [N] step, b [N] back, g N seek (clamped to 0..last), p play/pause toggle, p N play N cycles, q quit, empty line steps (or pauses while playing); any line pauses a play. Bad input shows a message line and does not end the command. Reason: stdlib has no raw terminal mode and x/term is a dependency (C13); raw keys are a later change needing owner approval.

records.title: Viewer play: injectable clock, EOF rules, --delay
records.body: S12 (C35). tui.Player has no clock: the owner calls Tick once per frame while playing; pit view ticks every --delay ms (default 100) via an injectable after func. p plays to the last cycle and then pauses; play at the last cycle does nothing; p N plays N cycles. At end of input an open-ended play stops at once and a counted play (p N) finishes first, so piped scripts use p N and stay deterministic. Reason: testable play that always terminates.

records.title: Viewer layout: 72x20 grid, blocks of cells, reverse video
records.body: S12 (C35). The core is drawn as a grid of at most --cols x --rows characters (default 72x20, clamped to 1000), one character per cell when the core fits and otherwise per block of ceil(N/(cols*rows)) cells, rows labelled with the first address. A character shows the written owner with most cells in its block (lowest id on a tie) as a base-35 glyph (1-9, a-z, repeating) in one of 12 ANSI colours; '.' is unwritten; a block holding an executed address is reverse video. Bot lines (max 8) give live count and pc. Reason: 8000 cells need one 80x24 screen to watch a match; paging hides the action; flags let a bigger terminal show more.

records.title: pit view plumbing: runIn(args, stdin, stdout, stderr)
records.body: S12 (C35). cmd/pit gains runIn, run with a stdin reader; run(args, stdout, stderr) stays and passes an empty reader, so existing tests and the AGENTS.md signature hold. Reason: pit view is the first command that reads input and tests must feed it a strings.Reader.

records.title: Viewer fixture: imp vs dwarf, seed 24, core 24, 12 cycles
records.body: S12 (C35). testdata/viewer/fixture.jsonl = pit run bots/imp.s bots/dwarf.s --seed 24 --core-size 24 --min-separation 3 --cycle-limit 40 --replay FILE (a test regenerates it byte for byte). Core of 24 cells, imp at 3 (copies itself one cell ahead each cycle, so it reaches 14 and never wraps the core end), dwarf at 19 with its pointer cell at 22. The dwarf's bombs wrap the core end (22 + 4k mod 24), the one at cycle 11 lands on 14, the imp's newest copy, and at cycle 12 the imp executes that bomb and dies (live 0 against 1, bot 2 wins). Reason: small enough to derive every frame by hand, with writes by both bots, a bomb overwriting an imp copy, a wrapping write and a death.

records.title: S15 (C35): pit serve command shape
records.body: S15 (C35). 'pit serve [--port N] [--replays DIR] [--web DIR]' (net/http, stdlib) always binds 127.0.0.1 (default port 8080, 0 = free port), serves the viewer at / and the --replays directory at /replays/. Directories are opened as os.Root, so .. and symlinks cannot leave them (a refused path is 404). Only GET and HEAD are served (405 with Allow otherwise), and a request whose Host is not loopback or localhost gets 403 with no body (DNS-rebinding guard). Ctrl-C stops it. Reason: the smallest stdlib option that works around browsers blocking fetch from file://; loopback only means no flag can expose files to the network; S14 reuses newServeHandler.

records.title: S15 (C35): web viewer embedded into pit, not shipped beside it
records.body: S15 (C35). web/embed.go (package web, go:embed index.html style.css js) embeds the viewer files into the pit binary, excluding web/test; 'pit serve --web DIR' serves from disk instead for development. Reason: release archives hold one binary with no path to find web/ from, and embedding needs no change to scripts/build-release.sh.

records.title: S15 (C35): web viewer layout, colors, replay loading and test run
records.body: S15 (C35). Canvas: the core as square tiles in address order, tile colour per bot from last-writer id (golden-angle hues, hsl), empty cells dark grey, cells executed this cycle outlined in white (white tile if tiles are under 5 px); a core with more cells than pixels shows one tile per block of cells with the owner holding most cells, lowest id on a tie (as the terminal viewer). Side panel: per-bot live count and executed pc. Controls: first/back/play-pause/forward/last, speed (cycles per second), seek slider, keys Space/arrows/Home/End. Replay chosen with a file input, or '?replay=URL'. JS tests: 'node --test web/test/*.test.js' (node:test, shell glob). There is no package.json, so the Node must run .js files with ES module syntax by module-syntax detection: Node 26.12.0 is verified, older versions are not; CI runs the tests with the runner's Node and prints node --version. Reason: spec leaves layout open; the Go terminal viewer's block rule and frame model are the reference.

records.title: S15 (C35): JS replay parser strictness
records.body: S15 (C35). web/js/replay.js checks the line grammar and order, bot ids, address ranges, consecutive cycles, load cell counts and the end line against the cycles, and rejects other versions with 'replay: unsupported version N (this reader reads version 1)'. Config and bot-length ranges follow docs/spec/match.md section 1: core_size 1..1048576, max_processes 1..1048576, min_separation 0..1048576, cycle_limit 1..2^31-1, bot length 1..1048576, so a file cannot make the model allocate a huge core. It does not check exact writer bytes, placement consistency or that a bot steps only while live (the note from S11), so the model shows what is recorded. Live count = 1 + spawns - deaths, unclamped internally, shown as max(0, n) (as internal/tui). Reason: the viewer must not refuse files the Go reader accepts but should not trust ranges it indexes or allocates with.

records.title: Acceptance tests (internal/acceptance) build and run the real pit binary
records.body: TestMain builds ./cmd/pit with go build and the tests exec it from the repo root, because package main cannot be imported and the criteria name the command; goldens are internal/acceptance/testdata/imp_dwarf_seed1.result.txt and .hash.txt, and the golden hash is also compared with fullHash in internal/replay/replay_test.go.

records.title: Second shared viewer fixture with SPL: testdata/viewer/spl_fixture.jsonl and spl_frames.json
records.body: frames.json had no spawn or death, so live-process parity of the Go and web viewers was unchecked; the pair is written by pit run from testdata/viewer/spl_splitter.s and spl_sitter.s (seed 1, core 24), its frames derived by hand, and read by internal/tui TestFrames and web/test/model.test.js.

records.title: Flag interleaving and -- in pit run, tourney and view
records.body: cmd/pit parseInterleaved splits args with the flag package's own rules before one Parse: a non-bool flag without =value takes the next argument as its value even if that is --, and only a -- in a flag position ends the flags. One helper replaces three copies (run, tourney, view). Reason: the old test for a consumed -- could not tell a terminator from a flag value, so --replay -- turned later flags into files.

records.title: Replays are written through a temp file and rename
records.body: pit run --replay writes to .NAME.tmpPID.N in the same directory, syncs it and renames it over FILE, removing the temp on any failure, so FILE is never partial. A replaced regular file keeps its mode (the temp file is chmodded to it before the rename); a new file gets 0644 less the umask. A target that exists and is not a regular file (symlink, device, pipe) is written in place, because a rename would replace it. Reason: atomic result for files, no surprise for /dev/null or links, and no mode change on overwrite.

records.title: Tournament events-off path is a nil observer, not new API
records.body: tourney.play calls arena.RunObserved(cfg, bots, nil), which already keeps only one cycle of events; arena.Run is the one that keeps all events. TestRunKeepsNoEvents measures tourney.Run allocating about 1.38 MB for 6 matches (two imps that tie at 80000 cycles and a bot that dies at once, one round) against 11.5 MB for the events of the same matches kept by arena.Run. No new arena function; unexported tourney.playMatch is the test seam for the concurrency test. Reason: smallest change that removes the memory growth.

records.title: Arena limits exported and shared with replay
records.body: arena exports MaxCoreSize (= vm.MaxCoreSize), MaxCycleLimit, MaxMaxProcesses, MaxMinSeparation, MaxBots, MaxBotLength; internal/replay reads them instead of keeping copies. Reason: one source for the match.md section 1 limits.

records.title: pit view skips command lines over 64 KiB with a message
records.body: pit view reads input with a bufio.Reader instead of bufio.Scanner; a line of more than 65536 bytes (without the line break) is read to its end, ignored, shows 'line too long' on screen, and the session goes on (exit 0). Reason: bounded memory, and a pasted long line no longer ends the session with 'token too long'.

records.title: pit serve accepts Host localhost. with the root dot
records.body: isLocalHost trims one trailing dot before comparing with localhost (RFC 1034 root form of the same name). Other names with a dot, and 127.0.0.1., stay refused. Reason: same name, no rebinding risk added.

records.title: Acceptance package keeps no doc.go; package comment moves to acceptance_test.go
records.body: S23 (C35). internal/acceptance/doc.go is deleted and its package comment now heads acceptance_test.go, so the directory holds only _test.go files, as README.md and AGENTS.md say (test-only). go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... are unchanged. Reason: the file existed only to carry the package comment, and a non-test file contradicted 'test-only'.

records.title: asm.md bomber listing is an asm block under TestRoundTripSpecExamples
records.body: S23 (C35). The listing printed by pit asm for the bomber in docs/spec/asm.md section 9 is tagged asm, not text, because a listing is itself valid source (asm.md section 9). TestRoundTripSpecExamples now round-trips it and counts 5 asm blocks in asm.md; TestSpecListing checks that the asm block after the bomber equals the output of pit asm. Reason: one place checks every runnable listing in the specs; the text tag left it covered by a string comparison only.

records.title: S25 (C35): amends C103: pit serve takes POST /api/match; files stay GET and HEAD
records.body: S25 (C35). C103 allowed GET and HEAD only. Now POST is accepted at /api/match alone (the match endpoint); the viewer, /replays/ and /api/list stay GET and HEAD (405 with Allow otherwise). POST, not GET with a query, because a match is work that changes nothing but costs CPU, and a GET can be fired by any page through an image or link; POST needs the Content-Type application/json (so a form on another site cannot send it and a fetch from another site needs a preflight, which the server never answers), an Origin equal to the request Host over http if the header is sent, and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or none if sent. The 127.0.0.1 bind and the Host guard (403, empty body) are unchanged. Reason: the page must ask the server to run a match, and these checks keep another site from using the loopback server for that.

records.title: S25 (C35): pit serve API: GET /api/list and POST /api/match, JSON shapes and limits
records.body: S25 (C35). cmd/pit/serveapi.go, built for reuse by pit play (newAPI(bots, replays fs.FS, apiLimits), mount(mux), match(first, second, seed) returning the replay bytes or an *apiError). GET /api/list -> {"bots":[names ending .s],"replays":[names ending .jsonl],"truncated":true only if cut}: regular files only, base names, sorted, a symlink listed only if os.Root can open it, never a path; names with control characters or invalid UTF-8 skipped. POST /api/match {"bots":[A,B],"seed":"N"} (exactly two names from the listing, matched against the listing and never joined into a path; seed a decimal string 0..2^64-1, absent = 0 like pit run) -> 200 application/x-ndjson, the bytes pit run --replay writes with the default configuration; errors are JSON {error, and for a source error bot, line, col, message}: 400 bad request, 403 foreign Origin, 404 name not listed, 413 body over 4096 bytes, 415 not application/json, 422 assembler error (message names the listed file, no directory) or a match the arena refuses or a bot file over 64 KiB, 503 with Retry-After while another match runs. Limits: one match at a time, cycle limit 80000 (the pit run default; no request field changes the configuration), at most 1000 names per list. Reason: smallest shape the start page needs; seed as a string because JavaScript numbers lose precision above 2^53; limits keep one request from costing more than a default pit run.

records.title: S25 (C35): pit serve --bots DIR (default bots if present); start page behaviour
records.body: S25 (C35). pit serve gains --bots DIR, opened as an os.Root like --replays; without the flag it is bots under the working directory if that is a directory, else none (the page then shows only the replays and the file picker); an explicit missing directory is exit 1. Start page (web/js/home.js, wired in main.js): imp and dwarf preselected if listed; the seed field starts random and shown, a seed the page chose is replaced by a new random one at each Fight (so Fight twice gives two matches), a seed the user typed is kept; Fight and a click on a listed replay start playing at once, ?replay=URL still loads paused. Reason: the owner wants to run and watch a match in one step; a stale seed would repeat the same match.
